Chapter One

The Year Everything Changed

Emily & James · Our Story

It started in college.

James and the girl who would later become such an important part of his life were studying together. At first, there was nothing unusual about it. They were just two students who saw each other regularly, attended classes, talked sometimes, and went on with their normal lives.

But slowly, things changed for James.

He started noticing her more than he noticed everyone else. He looked forward to seeing her at college. Small conversations started meaning more to him. Even when they were not talking, just having her around was enough to make his day feel different.

He realized that he had fallen in love with her.

So instead of keeping his feelings to himself, James decided to approach her. He told her how he felt, and after some time, she agreed to be with him.

For James, that was enough.

He did not enter the relationship expecting it to end. He genuinely believed he had found someone he could love and build something real with.

There was something James already knew, though.

Before him, she had been involved with one of his friends, and she had already hurt him by talking to another boy and crossing the boundaries of that relationship.

James knew about it.

He could have walked away.

He could have told himself that if she had done it once, she might do it again.

But James was in love, and he chose to believe that things would be different with him.

He accepted her anyway.

He gave her his time. He gave her attention. He tried to be there whenever she needed him. He spent money on her, helped her when he could, and kept forgiving things that hurt him because he did not want to lose the person he loved.

Whenever something happened between them, James tried to make things work instead of ending everything.

Maybe that was one of his biggest mistakes.

He kept believing that love meant giving someone another chance.

Then another.

And another.

But slowly, the same problems started appearing.

She talked to other boys, and James would get hurt. When he tried to talk about it, instead of feeling understood, he often ended up being blamed.

There were times when she made mistakes, but somehow James became the one who was wrong.

They would argue about it, and James would try to explain why he was hurt. He was not asking for perfection. He wanted honesty and respect from the person he had chosen to love.

But their arguments became more frequent.

The more James tried to hold on, the more tired he became.

Still, he stayed.

He had already invested so much of himself into the relationship that leaving did not feel easy. He remembered the good moments. He remembered why he had fallen in love with her in the first place.

So he kept hoping that things would get better.

They did not.

Eventually, the arguments became too much. One argument turned into another, and the same problems kept coming back. James felt like he was being blamed for things he had not done, while the things that hurt him were being ignored.

Then she called him rude and disrespectful.

And she left.

Just like that, the relationship that James had tried so hard to save was over.

For James, it was not simply losing a girlfriend.

It felt like losing all the time, money, effort, patience, and love he had given to someone who had never truly valued it in the same way.

He had accepted her even after knowing what had happened before him.

He had trusted her.

He had stayed when leaving would have been easier.

And in the end, he was the one left feeling like he had been used.

After the breakup, James changed.

He became quieter. He did not trust people the same way anymore. The things that had happened stayed in his mind, even when he tried not to think about them.

And then there was Emily.

Emily had been living in the same apartment building. James lived upstairs, while Emily lived downstairs. They had been around each other for some time, but James had never imagined that she would become such an important person in his life.

The funny thing was that Emily had liked James before.

James knew that she had some interest in him, but at that time, he did not feel the same way.

There were things about Emily's behavior that James did not like. He had his own reasons for keeping his distance, and he never thought of her as someone he would eventually fall in love with.

Life had other plans.

After his breakup, Emily was there.

She supported him.

She listened to him.

She did not try to force him to forget everything overnight. She simply stayed around and gave him the kind of attention he needed at a time when he was hurt.

Another girl who lived nearby also helped bring them closer.

Slowly, Emily and James started talking more.

At first, it did not feel like a love story.

It was just two people getting closer.

A conversation here.

A small joke there.

A little time spent together.

Then more.

James was still carrying the damage from his previous relationship, and without realizing it, he started bringing that pain into his relationship with Emily.

This is the part of the story James would understand much later.

The girl who had hurt him had changed the way he treated love.

He had complained about being ignored, but now he was the one who sometimes ignored Emily.

He had complained about not receiving time, but now he was the one making excuses.

He had wanted someone to stay when he was at his worst, but when Emily needed him, he sometimes left her alone.

There were times when Emily cried because of him.

And still, she stayed.

James did not understand her patience at first.

He thought she would eventually get tired and leave, just like everyone else.

But she did not.

She kept showing him that she cared.

She kept making an effort.

And slowly, something inside James started changing.

The first time Emily kissed him on the lips, it was more than just a kiss for him.

It was the moment he began to understand that his feelings for her were becoming real.

He had not expected it.

He had not planned it.

But he could not deny it anymore.

Emily was becoming important to him.

Their relationship was not perfect. They had their own problems, arguments, misunderstandings, and moments when things became difficult.

But there was something different about Emily.

She stayed.

They mostly met privately and kept many parts of their relationship between themselves. Even though their families knew about their relationship, there were still things that only Emily and James knew.

Over time, the two of them became closer.

James started realizing that Emily was not trying to replace what he had lost.

She was giving him something completely different.

Patience.

Time.

Care.

And a chance to become better than the person he had become after being hurt.

James had once believed that the biggest pain in his life was being left by someone he loved.

He did not know yet that another lesson was waiting for him.

Sometimes the person who saves you from the damage caused by someone else becomes the person you hurt because of that same damage.

Emily had entered his life when he was broken.

And without knowing it, she was about to become the person who taught him how to love again.

Chapter Two

What I Gave, What I Lost

Emily & James · Our Story

There was a time when I thought love was something you had to earn.

I thought if I gave someone enough of my time, enough of my attention, enough of my money, enough of myself, they would eventually understand how much they meant to me.

I was wrong.

In 2025, I was in a relationship that slowly became everything I was willing to give and everything the other person was willing to take.

I gave her my time. I gave her my attention. I helped her whenever she needed me. I spent money on her without thinking twice. Three or four times a week, I would take her out to eat or have something to drink, and I would pay for everything. At that time, I never stopped to think about how much I was spending. I just wanted her to be happy.

I thought that was what love was supposed to look like.

If she needed something, I tried to help.

If she was upset, I tried to fix it.

If we had an argument, I was usually the one trying to make things right again.

Even when I knew I wasn't the one who had done something wrong, I would still apologize.

There were moments when I was so afraid of losing her that I was willing to put my pride aside completely. I would beg her not to leave. I would say sorry just to keep the relationship from falling apart. I would have done almost anything to make her stay.

Looking back now, I realize something painful.

A relationship cannot survive forever when only one person is carrying it.

Her friends had started influencing her. Slowly, the way she looked at me changed. The things I did for her no longer seemed to matter. The effort I was making became something she expected instead of something she appreciated.

And I kept trying harder.

I thought maybe if I gave more, things would go back to the way they were.

They didn't.

One memory still hurts when I think about it.

It was her birthday.

My mother was sick at the time, but I still left her and went to be with the girl I was in a relationship with. I thought her birthday was important. I thought being there for her was something I had to do.

Later, my mother was hospitalized.

Even now, when I remember that, I don't just remember what happened between me and that girl.

I remember what I was willing to sacrifice for someone who eventually left.

That is probably one of the hardest things about looking back.

It isn't only that someone left you.

It is realizing how much of yourself you gave before they did.

When the relationship finally ended, I didn't know what to do with all the feelings that were left behind.

I cried.

A lot.

I remembered the conversations we had, the places we went, the times we ate together, the walks, the promises, and all the little things that had once felt like they would last forever.

I kept thinking about everything I had done and wondering how something I had given so much to could end so easily.

For a while, I felt completely alone.

I had spent so much time trying to keep someone else from leaving that I had forgotten how to take care of myself.

And then there was Emily.

She came into my life at a time when I wasn't really okay.

She lived in the same apartment building. I was upstairs and she was downstairs.

The strange thing was that Emily had liked me before all of this.

But I didn't see her that way at first.

I had my own opinions about her. There were things about her behavior that I didn't like, and I never imagined that she would become the person who would mean so much to me later.

At that point, I wasn't looking for another relationship.

Honestly, I wasn't even sure I wanted to trust anyone again.

I was hurt.

I was angry.

And I had started believing that maybe caring too much about someone was just another way of giving them the power to hurt you.

Emily didn't try to force herself into my life.

She was just there.

When I was upset, she listened.

When I wanted to talk, she listened.

When I didn't know what to say, she still stayed.

I was carrying so much anger and sadness from what had happened that sometimes I didn't even know how to explain what was wrong with me.

But Emily didn't need me to explain everything perfectly.

She tried to understand me anyway.

There were times when I cried in front of her.

Times when I was frustrated.

Times when I was difficult.

And I know I wasn't always fair to her.

I had been hurt by someone else, but I was carrying that hurt into something new.

Sometimes I would ignore Emily.

Sometimes I would make excuses.

Sometimes I wouldn't give her the time she deserved.

There were moments when I probably made her feel like she wasn't important to me.

And she cried because of me.

That is something I can never pretend didn't happen.

The person who had come into my life when I was broken was now getting hurt because of the broken parts of me.

I didn't understand it fully at the time.

I was still too lost in everything that had happened before.

But Emily stayed.

She didn't suddenly become perfect, and our relationship wasn't perfect either.

We argued.

We misunderstood each other.

We had our own problems.

But there was something different about her.

She didn't make me feel like I had to earn her care.

She cared because she cared.

She would calm me down when I was upset.

She would explain things to me when I didn't understand.

She would listen even when I was repeating the same things again and again.

Sometimes it felt like she was taking care of me more than I deserved.

She treated me almost like I was her own child.

And even when I bothered her, even when I was difficult, she didn't make me feel worthless.

That meant more to me than I knew how to say.

There was a point when I started noticing the difference between what I had been chasing and what I actually needed.

I had spent so much time trying to convince someone to stay.

Emily never made me beg.

I had spent money trying to make someone happy.

Emily was happy just having me around.

I had given everything I could to someone who slowly stopped valuing it.

Emily was giving me something I couldn't buy.

Patience.

Understanding.

Care.

She was giving me a reason to believe that maybe love wasn't supposed to feel like constantly being afraid of losing someone.

Then came the moment that changed something inside me.

Our first kiss on the lips.

It wasn't some huge movie moment.

But for me, it meant something.

Because after everything I had been through, I realized that what I felt for Emily was real.

I wasn't talking to her just because I was lonely.

I wasn't staying because I needed someone to replace the person who had left.

I was beginning to love her.

And that scared me.

Because when you've already lost someone you gave everything to, loving someone again means giving them the same power to hurt you.

But this time, something was different.

Emily wasn't asking me to prove my love by destroying myself for her.

She was simply there.

And slowly, I started understanding what I had failed to understand before.

Love isn't always about how much you can give.

Sometimes love is about the person who stays beside you when you don't have anything left to give.

Emily had seen me at one of my lowest points.

She had seen the angry side of me.

The sad side.

The confused side.

The side that didn't know how to trust anymore.

And somehow, she still chose to stay.

I don't think I understood the weight of that choice back then.

I understand it now.

Because she didn't just become my girlfriend.

She became the person who helped me become myself again.

She taught me that being cared for doesn't always come with a price.

That someone can listen without expecting something in return.

That someone can stay without being begged.

And most importantly, she taught me that sometimes the person who comes into your life after you've been hurt doesn't deserve the punishment for what someone else did.

I wish I had understood that sooner.

Because Emily gave me the kind of patience I had once begged someone else for.

And while she was trying to heal the parts of me that someone else had broken, I was sometimes hurting her with those same broken parts.

That is something I will always regret.

But maybe that is what made our story real.

We weren't perfect.

We didn't suddenly become the perfect couple.

We were two people trying to understand each other while carrying our own problems, our own mistakes, and our own fears.

And somewhere in all of that, I realized something.

I had spent so much time thinking about the person I lost that I almost failed to see the person who had stayed.

Emily was there when I had nothing left.

And somehow, she made me feel like maybe I hadn't lost everything after all.

Maybe I had just lost the wrong person.

And found the right one.

Chapter Three

When She Walked Away

Emily & James · Our Story

There are some days you remember because they were beautiful.

And then there are days you remember because they changed something inside you.

For me, one of those days started like any other college day.

There had been a project at college, something we had all worked on together. When the project was finally completed, we received trophies for it. At that moment, none of us were thinking about problems, relationships, misunderstandings, or what might happen later.

We were just happy.

We took pictures with the trophies. We laughed with our friends. For a little while, everything felt simple.

Afterward, all of us decided to go to McDonald's to celebrate.

I remember that happiness because it felt innocent. We were just a group of friends who had achieved something together, sitting around, talking, laughing, and enjoying the fact that our hard work had paid off.

She was there too.

I kept looking at her without making it obvious.

Even when we were surrounded by people, part of my attention always stayed with her.

I had become the kind of person who noticed the smallest things about her. Her expressions. Her smile. Whether she looked happy. Whether something was bothering her.

I did not need a reason to care about her.

I just did.

There was another day when we all went to our friend's house. I will call her Sophie here.

Everyone went together, and the whole day felt different from the usual college routine. We sat together, talked about random things, laughed, and took a lot of pictures.

I had brought a gift for her too.

Giving her something had become normal for me.

Whenever I met her, I tried to bring something. It did not always have to be expensive or important. Sometimes the value of a gift is not in what it costs. Sometimes you give something because you want to see a particular smile.

That was what I was looking for every time.

Her happiness.

I think I was always searching for that happiness because somewhere inside me, I was still starving for it myself.

If giving her something could make her happy, then for a moment, I felt happy too.

That day, she spent a lot of time with us.

We talked.

We laughed.

There were so many conversations that, at the time, felt completely ordinary.

But looking back, ordinary moments can become the ones you miss the most.

Eventually, it was time for everyone to go home.

I went in my car.

She left with two of my male friends in their car.

Nothing about that seemed unusual to me.

We were all friends.

She was going home, and I was going home.

That should have been the end of the day.

But sometimes a normal day can become the beginning of something you never expected.

On the way home, I talked to one of my friends.

It was just a conversation.

Nothing more.

I did not know that somewhere between what I said and what was understood, something had gone terribly wrong.

She somehow got the impression that I had been insulting her on the phone.

That I had been abusing her.

That I had said things about her that I would never have said.

But I had not.

That was the part that broke me.

Because I loved her.

Whatever problems existed between us, whatever arguments we had, whatever mistakes either of us had made, there was one thing I knew about myself.

I could never intentionally say something hateful about her.

I could be angry.

I could be hurt.

I could be confused.

But I could not stand there and destroy the person I loved with words.

Yet somehow, that was exactly what she believed I had done.

When she reached home, I expected her to talk to me.

I waited for her message.

Nothing came.

I sent one message.

Then another.

Then another.

No response.

I kept checking my phone.

Nothing.

I started asking my friends whether she had reached home safely.

They told me she had.

She was home.

She was fine.

But she was not talking to me.

That difference destroyed me.

Because if something had happened to her, at least I would have known why she was silent.

But she was okay.

She was talking to other people.

She was answering others.

She just was not answering me.

And I could not understand why.

I kept staring at my phone as if the screen could somehow give me an answer.

Maybe she would reply in a few minutes.

Maybe she was angry and needed some time.

Maybe she had misunderstood something and would eventually ask me what had happened.

I kept creating explanations because accepting the silence was harder.

I cried.

I was genuinely lost.

I did not know what to do.

When you love someone deeply, losing communication with them can feel worse than an argument.

At least an argument gives you something to fight against.

Silence gives you nothing.

There is no sentence to answer.

No accusation to explain.

No door to knock on.

Just silence.

I wanted to fix everything.

I wanted to tell her that I had not abused her.

I wanted her to hear my side.

I wanted her to know that the person she thought I had become was not who I was.

I spoke to her sister.

Instead of helping me understand what had happened, the conversation became even worse.

She accused me of abusing her.

She spoke to me harshly.

She even threatened me.

I was already broken because the person I loved would not speak to me, and now I was standing in front of another person trying to defend something I had never done.

But I was so attached to that relationship that even then, I did not want a fight.

I apologized.

I kept asking for forgiveness.

Not because I believed I had done what they were accusing me of, but because I was desperate to stop everything from falling apart.

There is a strange kind of helplessness that comes with loving someone more than you love your own pride.

You stop asking, "Am I right?"

You start asking, "What can I do to make this person stay?"

I reached that point.

I was willing to say sorry for something I had not done just because I thought maybe the apology would bring her back to me.

I asked for another chance.

I wanted to talk to her.

I wanted her to listen.

At one point, I even said that I was willing to fall at her feet and apologize if that was what it took to make her believe me.

That was how far I had gone.

Not because I had no self respect.

Because at that time, I was terrified of losing her.

Then I spoke to her sister again.

The threats continued.

I remember feeling angry, but underneath that anger was fear.

Fear that a misunderstanding was becoming bigger than the relationship itself.

Fear that no matter what I said, nobody wanted to hear me.

Fear that the person I loved had already decided who I was without asking me what had actually happened.

Eventually, I told them something I had never expected to say.

I told them that I had powerful connections and that I could get my own information and details verified if necessary.

I said I could make one call and provide whatever was needed to prove my side.

My point was simple.

If I had actually done something wrong, why would I be willing to put everything in front of them?

Why would I ask them to verify it?

Why would I keep trying to prove my innocence if I knew I was guilty?

I did not want to threaten anyone.

I wanted the truth.

That was all.

I wanted someone to stop for one moment and ask me what had actually happened.

But by then, everything had become bigger than one phone call.

It was no longer about a single misunderstanding.

It was about trust.

And once trust begins to disappear, even the truth can struggle to reach the other person.

I kept trying.

I kept messaging her.

I kept hoping that eventually she would reply.

Every time my phone lit up, my heart jumped.

Every time it was someone else, the disappointment felt heavier.

The strangest thing about heartbreak is that nothing around you changes.

The same room is still there.

The same phone is in your hand.

The same people are walking around you.

The same world continues as if nothing happened.

But inside you, everything feels different.

That night, I learned something I did not understand before.

Sometimes you do not lose someone because you stopped loving them.

Sometimes you lose them while you are still doing everything you can to hold on.

I was still trying.

Still explaining.

Still apologizing.

Still waiting.

But she was already moving further away.

And no matter how many messages I sent, I could not make someone listen when they had already chosen silence.

I wish I could say I understood everything that night.

I did not.

I only knew that I loved her, I believed I had been misunderstood, and I was terrified that this misunderstanding would become the reason she walked out of my life.

I did not know then that this was not going to be the last time I would have to learn what it feels like when someone you love chooses to leave.

I only knew that something between us had changed.

And for the first time, I could feel the distance.

Not the kind of distance measured in roads or kilometers.

A different kind.

The kind that begins when two people are still close enough to reach each other, but one of them no longer wants to reach back.

That was the beginning of the end.

And I was still standing there, trying to save something that was already slipping through my hands.

Chapter Four

The Girl Who Found Me Broken

Emily & James · Our Story

After my first relationship ended, I was not the same person anymore.

I had become quiet.

Not the kind of quiet where someone simply has nothing to say. I was quiet because I did not know what to say. I had so much going on inside me that even talking to people started to feel irritating. If someone tried to talk to me, I would sometimes get angry for no real reason. I became short-tempered, frustrated, and difficult to understand.

I was hurting, but I did not know how to explain that pain.

From the outside, it probably looked like I was just angry all the time. But inside, I was trying to deal with the feeling of being left behind by someone I had trusted.

I wanted to move on.

More than anything, I wanted to prove that I could.

That was when Emily entered my life.

She did not come into my life through some big plan. We were introduced because of one of our neighbors. She was the person who connected us on Instagram, and that was where Emily and I first started talking.

I sent the first message because my friend had told me to.

At that time, I did not know where that one message would take me.

I did not know that a simple conversation on Instagram would eventually become one of the most important parts of my life.

Emily and I had not known each other for years. There was no long friendship before our relationship. There was no story behind us before that first conversation.

There was just one message.

Then another.

And then somehow, we started talking more.

I think one reason I became close to her so quickly was because I was still trying to escape my pain.

I wanted to feel like I had moved on.

I wanted to show myself that I could start again.

At first, that was probably more important to me than I realized.

Emily and I entered a relationship very quickly. We did not spend months trying to figure out what we were. Somehow, after we started talking, we became a relationship before either of us really understood how it happened.

For the first few days, everything felt good.

We talked.

We laughed.

We got to know each other.

For a while, it felt like I had finally found something that could take my mind away from everything that had happened before.

But there was still a part of me that was broken.

And broken people do not always know how to love someone properly.

After those first good days, I started doing something that I still think about.

I started hurting Emily.

Not because she had done something to deserve it.

Not because I did not care about her.

I was simply carrying so much anger and confusion from my previous relationship that I started behaving with Emily in ways that were unfair to her.

I would get angry.

I would ignore her.

Sometimes I would stop talking to her.

Sometimes I would hurt her with my behavior without thinking about what it would do to her.

And the worst part was that I was doing to her some of the same things that had once hurt me.

The person who had once been hurt by being ignored was now ignoring someone else.

The person who had once hated feeling unwanted was making someone else feel unwanted.

At that time, I did not fully understand what I was doing.

I was still trying to figure myself out.

But Emily understood something that I did not.

She understood that behind my anger, there was pain.

She knew I was not always easy to deal with.

She saw the version of me that other people probably would not have wanted to stay around.

Yet she stayed.

That is what slowly changed everything for me.

Emily did not only tell me that she loved me.

She showed me.

Whenever I became angry with her, she would try to make things right.

If I became upset, she would try to calm me down.

If I stopped talking, she would come back and try to make me talk.

She would say things that made me smile when I did not want to smile.

She would talk to me with love when I was giving her reasons to be angry.

She would try to fix my mood instead of making it worse.

And she kept doing it.

Again and again.

That was something I had never expected.

I was used to thinking that when you hurt someone, eventually they leave.

I was used to thinking that when someone gets tired of your behavior, they stop caring.

But Emily was different.

Even when I became angry with her, she could not simply stay away from me.

She would come back and try to make me happy.

She would say good things to me.

She would love me when I was not making it easy for her to love me.

And somehow, she knew how to bring my mood back.

That kind of care started becoming impossible for me to ignore.

I had spent so much time thinking about the person who had left me that I had failed to notice the person who was standing right in front of me.

Emily was not asking me to become perfect.

She was simply staying.

And that meant more to me than I knew how to explain.

There was another thing that happened between us that I still remember.

While Emily and I were already in a relationship, I had talked to my cousins about one of them. I had praised her a lot and, as a joke, said things about getting me set up with her. I did not mean it seriously.

But Emily saw those messages.

She became upset and distant.

And honestly, I understood why.

From her side, it did not look like a harmless joke.

She had every reason to feel hurt.

I knew that I had crossed a line, even if I had not intended it in the way it looked.

That moment could have ended everything.

Someone else might have decided that enough was enough.

Someone else might have walked away.

But Emily eventually forgave me.

I do not think I understood the value of that forgiveness immediately.

At that time, I probably just felt relieved that she was still with me.

But later, I realized what it meant.

She had already seen my anger.

She had already experienced my ignoring her.

She had already been hurt by my behavior.

And now she had another reason to leave.

Still, she chose not to.

That was when I started asking myself a question.

How many times can someone forgive you and still choose you?

And why was Emily still choosing me?

The answer was becoming clearer.

She genuinely cared about me.

Not the version of me that I wanted everyone else to see.

The real me.

The difficult me.

The angry me.

The broken me.

She had met me at a time when I was not at my best.

And instead of waiting for me to become perfect, she stayed while I was still trying to put myself back together.

That changed the way I looked at her.

At first, I had entered the relationship because I wanted to move on.

Then I stayed because I started caring.

Then I became attached because of everything she did for me.

And eventually, I realized that I did not want to lose her.

That realization came quietly.

There was no dramatic moment.

It was simply something I started feeling every time she came back after I pushed her away.

Every time she tried to make me smile.

Every time she showed me love.

Every time she stayed.

I started thinking about how different my life would feel if she was not there.

And that thought scared me.

Because by then, Emily was no longer just someone I was talking to.

She had become part of my everyday life.

She had become someone I expected to be there.

Someone whose absence would actually hurt me.

Someone I had started needing, not because I wanted to use her to forget my past, but because I genuinely loved what she had become in my life.

That was when I finally admitted something to myself.

I did not want to lose her.

I remember thinking that after everything she had done for me, after all the times she had stayed, after all the love and care she had given me, I could not imagine simply going back to life without her.

She had become my life.

And maybe that was the biggest difference between the beginning of our relationship and what it had become.

At the beginning, I was trying to use the relationship to prove that I had moved on.

By the end of this part of our story, I was no longer thinking about proving anything to anyone.

I was thinking about Emily.

I was thinking about us.

I was thinking about how someone I had met through a simple Instagram conversation had somehow become the person I did not want to lose.

I had started talking to her because my friend told me to send that first message.

I had entered the relationship because I wanted to push away my pain.

But somewhere between those first messages and all the difficult days that followed, something real had happened.

I had found someone who stayed.

Someone who forgave.

Someone who cared.

Someone who made efforts for me even when she had every reason not to.

And most importantly, I had found someone who saw me broken and still believed I was worth loving.

I had once thought that moving on meant forgetting the person who had hurt me.

Emily taught me something different.

Sometimes moving on does not happen because you forget the past.

Sometimes it happens because someone new enters your life and slowly shows you that love does not always have to feel like abandonment.

Emily did not erase everything that had happened to me.

She simply gave me something else to hold on to.

And without even realizing it, I stopped looking backward.

I started looking at her.

And for the first time after everything that had happened, I had someone I truly did not want to lose.
